title: What If You Never Slept Again?
sources: National Sleep Foundation / CDC: sleep deprivation impairs focus, memory and immune function within days
Randy Gardner, 1964: 264 hours (11 days) without sleep, the documented record
Fatal familial insomnia: a rare genetic disease where total sleep loss is eventually fatal

lines.text: What would happen if you never slept again?
The first night, your brain starts fighting you.
By day two, you can't focus, and your memory starts slipping.
By day three, you start hallucinating things that aren't there.
Your body stops repairing itself, and your immune system crashes.
Your heart races, and your blood pressure climbs.
After a week, your brain starts shutting down parts of itself.
In rare cases, people have died from extreme sleep loss.
The record is eleven days, and he was never the same.
So why do we sleep? Scientists still don't fully know.
But while you rest, your brain flushes out its waste.
So maybe... just go to sleep.
